summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, gastroparesis, anxiety, and chronic abdominal pain was admitted for acute-on-chronic abdominal pain and vomiting, consistent with a gastroparesis flare. She was treated with IV fluids, anti-nausea medications, and pain control. Labs revealed iron deficiency anemia, low B12 and folate, and chronic leukocytosis, prompting IV iron and supplementation. Her kidney function improved with hydration. She tolerated oral intake within 48 hours and was discharged home in stable condition. Insulin was adjusted downward, and she was advised to follow up with her primary care provider for medication titration, EKG monitoring for prolonged QTc, and outpatient iron management.
